files.purpose: Main game logic, Pygame setup, game loop, event handling, rendering.
Classes for Mouse, Cat, and Crumb entities.

assets.strategy_rationale: The spec explicitly states 'plain coloured shapes only; no images or sounds', so all assets will be drawn programmatically.

architecture.test_input_example: Press RIGHT, then UP, then LEFT, then DOWN to navigate the maze. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.

decisions.reason: The spec requires visual elements (grid, mouse, cats, crumbs) but explicitly forbids images and sounds, making pygame with procedural drawing the most suitable renderer. Terminal rendering would be too limited for the visual detail implied.
A standard resolution chosen to comfortably display a 15x15 grid and UI elements.
A standard frame rate for smooth real-time gameplay.
This algorithm generates a perfect maze (no loops, every part reachable) which is suitable for a simple grid maze game and ensures all crumbs are accessible.

The spec says 'at each junction picks a direction toward the mouse'. Manhattan distance is a simple heuristic for 'toward' in a grid and is computationally inexpensive. Cats will not have full pathfinding but will make local optimal choices.

decisions.choice: Instantaneous tile-to-tile movement upon direction change, then continuous until wall
decisions.reason: The spec says 'it keeps moving tile by tile in that direction until it hits a wall'. This implies a continuous movement rather than step-by-step input, but the initial 'turn' implies an immediate change of direction.

decisions.choice: Mouse starts at (0,0), cats at (14,14) and (0,14)
decisions.reason: The spec does not specify starting positions. These choices provide distinct starting points for the mouse and cats, ensuring immediate interaction is not guaranteed but also not impossible.
For a 15x15 grid, 40x40 pixel tiles fit well within an 800x600 window, leaving space for UI elements.

decisions.choice: Score and Lives displayed at the top center of the screen.
decisions.reason: The spec says 'at the top of the window'. Centering them provides a clean layout.
